h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבַּת תְּשׁוּבָה, ז׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 7

p: "Let the wicked forsake his way," etc.,
"and let him return to Hashem, and He will have mercy on him,
and to our God, for He will abundantly forgive.
For My thoughts are not your thoughts," etc.
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמַר וְיָשׁוֹב אֶל ה׳ וְגוֹמֵר:
for what he said, "and let him return to Hashem," etc.:
The matter is that this refers
Sometimes, when a person knows about himself
that he has already repented and prayed,
that he has still not been saved,
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts,"
in the manner of what is said (Tehillim 92:6),
"Great" alludes to what is beyond measure,
the aspect of Peleh, the Wondrous;
שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ גַּם כֵּן נִפְלָאוּ,
of Hashem, blessed be He, are also wondrous,
"A boorish man does not know," etc.,
But in truth, the end is
that "the tzaddik will flourish like a date palm"
דְּאִיתָא (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב, ב):
as it is brought (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:2:2):
"My children, open for Me one opening
of teshuvah like the eye of a needle,
and I will open for you openings
through which wagons and carriages can enter."
Sometimes it seems to a person
שֶׁהוּא כְּבָר פָּתַח פֶּתַח שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה,
that he has already opened an opening of teshuvah,
and yet he has not been saved
so as to see the Heavenly help from Hashem, blessed be He.
And about this, too, it is said,
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts";
thoughts of peace and not of evil,
to give you a future and hope."
שֶׁכָּל הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלֵינוּ
For all of Hashem's thoughts concerning us
even though to the eye's view
just as in the Babylonian exile,
there they merited the principal spread
through the Men of the Great Assembly.
And sometimes even the distance is for good,
which comes to rectify the "much anger."
"And You will forgive my iniquity, for it is great"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים יט, טז):
מִפֶּשַׁע רָב, אוֹתוֹ עָוֹן רַב וְכוּלֵּי;
"'From great transgression' — that great iniquity," etc.;
that He can rectify even things
"Let the wicked forsake his way," etc.,
"and let him return to Hashem, and He will have mercy on him":
that He will open openings for him, etc.;
"and to our God, for He will abundantly forgive":
"And You will forgive my iniquity, for it is great,"
And this is the meaning of what they said
between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,"
אַף שֶׁבֵּין רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
though between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur
as they said in the holy Zohar
and it is not written 'in six.'"
and when he refines himself in the seven middos,
then Hashem, blessed be He, refines him
And this is what it says,
"and to our God, for He will abundantly forgive."
between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur
so that they are called ten days;
for always within these seven days
one is refined in the first three as well;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנז, א):
on account of the three supernal levels:
and she is the Bas, a fourth to them."
And through this one is refined
by means of the Shabbos within them.
